item.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
item.description:
CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

  • CVE-2026-114713 UnrealIRCd Improper Neutralization of Delimiters Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-123039 Check Point Multiple Products Incorrect Permission Assignment for Critical Resource Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

item.title: Siemens Desigo, Gridscale
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

On October 21, 2026, the Node.js project released security updates addressing a critical vulnerability in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, commonly referred to as "Node2Shell" (tracked as CVE-2026-111497). The vulnerability is an out-of-bounds write that could allow a remote attacker to cause memory corruption and potentially execute arbitrary code. This advisory covers the status of impact of various Siemens software products. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.

The following versions of Siemens Desigo, Gridscale are affected:

  • Desigo CC family V8 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-111497)
  • Desigo CC family V9 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-111497)
  • Gridscale X DSA vers:intdot/>=5.3|<5.4 (CVE-2026-111497)

  • Gridscale X PSS®E vers:intdot/<36.8.0 (CVE-2026-111497)

     

CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 9.8 Siemens Desigo CC family V8
1 Vulnerability
Out-of-bounds Write

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Energy, Information Technology
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-111497
A buffer overflow vulnerability in the Brotli decoder (c/dec/decode.c) in Google Brotli versions 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 on all platforms allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream. Users need to update any Brotli libraries or binaries between 1.0.3 through 1.2.0 to the latest available version: 1.0.10 or 1.1.1 or 1.2.1.
Read More

4 Affected Products

Desigo CC family V8

Product Status: known_affected, known_not_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Install the latest .NET security updates via Windows Update.

Desigo CC family V9

Product Status: known_affected, known_not_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Install the latest .NET security updates via Windows Update.

Gridscale X DSA >= V5.3 < V5.4

Product Status: known_affected, known_not_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Update to V5.4 or later version

Gridscale X PSS®E < V36.8.0

Product Status: known_affected, known_not_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Update to V36.8.0 or later version

Additional Metrics

Relevant CWE: CWE-787 Out-of-bounds Write

CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String
3.1 9.8 CRITICAL CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

View CVE Details

Acknowledgments

  • Siemens ProductCERT reported this vulnerability to CISA.

General Recommendations

Operators of critical power systems (e.g. TSOs or DSOs) worldwide are usually required by regulations to build resilience into the power grids by applying multi-level redundant secondary protection schemes. It is therefore recommended that the operators check whether appropriate resilient protection measures are in place. The risk of cyber incidents impacting the grid's reliability can thus be minimized by virtue of the grid design. Siemens strongly recommends applying the provided security updates using the corresponding tooling and documented procedures made available with the product. If supported by the product, an automated means to apply the security updates across multiple product instances may be used. Siemens strongly recommends prior validation of any security update before being applied, and supervision by trained staff of the update process in the target environment. As a general security measure Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access with appropriate mechanisms (e.g. firewalls, segmentation, VPN). It is advised to configure the environment according to our operational guidelines in order to run the devices in a protected IT environment. Recommended security guidelines can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/gridsecurity

Additional Resources

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories

Terms of Use

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

Advisory Conversion Disclaimer

This ICSA is a verbatim republication of Siemens ProductCERT SSA-045512 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. CISA is not responsible for the editorial or technical accuracy of republished advisories and provides no warranties of any kind regarding any information contained within this advisory. Further, CISA does not endorse any commercial product or service. Please contact Siemens ProductCERT directly for any questions regarding this advisory.

item.title: Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Palo Alto Networks has published information on vulnerabilities in PAN-OS related to PHP2Shell vulnerabilities. This advisory lists the related Siemens Industrial products affected by these vulnerabilities. Customers are advised to consult and implement the workarounds provided in Palo Alto Networks' upstream security notifications. 

The following versions of Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808 are affected:

  • RUGGEDCOM APE1808 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 9.8 Siemens RUGGEDCOM APE1808
1 Vulnerability
Use After Free

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-109618
PHP uses longjmp() for out-of-memory (OOM) errors to exit the current context and abort handling of the request. Some contexts may not properly account for this scenario and leave request memory in an uninitialized state before performing an allocation. The subsequent request cleanup procedure may read or branch on this memory. Multiple OOM strategies can consistently trigger this condition and lead to remote code execution (RCE).
Read More

1 Affected Product

RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (10.2 All, 11.1 All, 11.2 All, 12.1 All, 12.2 All)

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Upgrade to corresponding available PAN-OS version. Contact customer support to receive additional patch and update information.

Additional Metrics

Relevant CWE: CWE-416 Use After Free

CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String
3.1 9.8 CRITICAL CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-109619
PHP has various global state that temporarily points into request memory. In some scenarios, global state may not be correctly reset, or may be repopulated after being reset. The global state may then refer to request memory even after it has been freed. Subsequent requests may read or branch on this stale state before it is fully initialized. Multiple strategies can trigger this condition and produce remote code execution (RCE).
Read More

2 Affected Products

RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (10.2 All, 11.1 All, 11.2 All, 12.1 All, 12.2 All)

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Upgrade to corresponding available PAN-OS version. Contact customer support to receive additional patch and update information.

RUGGEDCOM APE1808 with Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (10.2 All, 11.1 All, 11.2 All, 12.1 All, 12.2 All)

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Upgrade to corresponding available PAN-OS version. Contact customer support to receive additional patch and update information.

Additional Metrics

Relevant CWE: CWE-416 Use After Free

CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String
3.1 8.1 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H

View CVE Details

General Recommendations

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Additional information on Industrial Security by Siemens can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/industrialsecurity

Additional Resources

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories

Terms of Use

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

item.title: Siemens Building Automation and Energy Products
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

On October 21, 2026, the PHP project and security researchers disclosed two critical, unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities in the core PHP language runtime known as "php2shell" (tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619). This advisory covers the status of impact of various Siemens software products. As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends to protect network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends to configure the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines, and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Siemens is actively monitoring the situation and assessing the implications of these vulnerabilities on our portfolio. Because this evaluation is ongoing, our findings are subject to change as new technical details and vendor updates emerge. We will publish updated findings, guidance, and remediation recommendations as soon as they become available. Siemens has released new versions for several affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions. Siemens is preparing further fixes and recommends mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens Building Automation and Energy Products are affected:

  • AMIS TS vers:all/* (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
  • blueplanet 360 NX3 M6 WM OD IISX vers:all/* (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)
  • blueplanet 360 NX3 M6 WM OD IISX - S vers:all/* (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619)

Recommended security guidelines can be found at: https://www.siemens.com/gridsecurity

Additional Resources

For further inquiries on security vulnerabilities in Siemens products and solutions, please contact the Siemens ProductCERT: https://www.siemens.com/cert/advisories

Terms of Use

The use of Siemens Security Advisories is subject to the terms and conditions listed on: https://www.siemens.com/productcert/terms-of-use.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

item.title: CISA Adds Six Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
item.description:
CISA has added six new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

  • CVE-2026-20320 Cisco BroadWorks Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-111560 Barracuda Networks Multiple Products OS Command Injection Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-111793 Openwave Messaging Limited Webtop Media Transcoder Incorrect Resource Transfer Between Spheres Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-116606 Barracuda Networks Email Security Gateway (ESG) Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-124194 Microsoft Office Outlook Missing User Interaction for Potentially Unsafe Action Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-125350 Google Chromium Use-After-Free Vulnerability 

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise.

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

item.title: US Government Partners Urge Hardening Industrial Refrigeration and Cold Chain Monitoring Systems
item.description:
Overview

The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), Health and Human Services (HHS), U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA), and the Department of Transportation (DoT)—hereafter referred to as “the authoring organizations”—are aware of malicious cyber activity targeting industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring systems globally. Organizations in the Healthcare and Public Health, Chemical, Food and Agriculture, and Transportation Systems Sectors widely use these systems, including in refrigerated transport services, for automated and remote monitoring of temperatures, continuous temperature logging, defrost cycle management, and energy optimization.

The authoring organizations urge owners and operators to defend against this activity by using strong authentication, keeping systems updated, identifying any systems that are accessible from the internet, removing unnecessary remote access, and securing any necessary remote access.

Threat

The authoring organizations are aware of malicious cyber actors targeting electronic temperature controllers and commercial refrigeration controllers in retail grocery and cold storage facilities. The actors may exploit vulnerabilities or weaknesses in unpatched or internet-accessible controllers to remotely alter settings and force units into continuous heating and defrost cycles, which can cause widespread inventory loss and equipment hazards.

Specifically, the actors may exploit these flaws through multiple vectors:

  • Authentication bypass;
  • Arbitrary code injection; and
  • Weak configurations.

Upon successful exploitation of the flaws, the actors could achieve the following effects:

  • Change of temperature, which could:
    • Affect the service life of the system;
    • Create a fire hazard;
    • Cause loss of inventory; or
    • Indirectly harm consumers if products are consumed after unsafe storage.
  • Loss of visibility into current temperatures (a denial-of-view condition).

Mitigations

The authoring organizations urge owners and operators to immediately take the following actions. These mitigations align with the Cross-Sector Cybersecurity Performance Goals (CPGs), developed by CISA and the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). The CPGs provide a minimum set of practices and protections that CISA and NIST recommend all organizations implement:

  • Eliminate public internet exposure: Do not expose control system devices and/or systems, particularly controller panels, to the internet [CPG 3.S]. Should remote access be necessary, protect it by using a firewall or edge device and updating it to the latest version to reduce security vulnerabilities. See CISA’s Internet Exposure Reduction Guidance and Defend the Edge: The Critical Importance of Edge Device Security for additional guidance on securing edge devices.
  • Isolate operational technology (OT) devices: Create a dedicated OT virtual local area network (VLAN) to separate OT devices from business networks [CPG 3.I].
  • Enforce credential security: Change default passwords [CPG 3.A], strengthen passwords, and implement strong password policies [CPG 3.B]. Further, implement phishing-resistant multifactor authentication wherever feasible [CPG 3.F].
  • Apply patches: Keep device firmware up to date and establish a structured lifecycle management process to identify, retire, and replace legacy devices that are at end of life (EOL) and no longer supported by the manufacturer [CPG 2.A, 2.B]. See CISA’s BOD 26-04: Implementation Guidance for Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk and BOD 26-02: Mitigating Risk From End-of-Support Edge Devices for additional guidance.
  • Restrict access: Define and maintain device and IP address allowlisting, limiting access to only those devices and IP addresses authorized to make changes [CPG 3.H].
  • Have reliable backups: Maintain current backups offsite and offline and test them [CPG 3.O].
  • Monitor and report: Enable logging [CPG 3.Q] and regularly review logs for unexpected activity.
    • For OT assets where logs are non-standard or not available, collect network traffic and communications between the assets.
  • Review setpoint ranges: Define and maintain reasonable setpoint limits for devices operating downstream of controllers to stay within safe ranges and establish alerting for deviations.

Resources

The authoring organizations strongly urge industrial refrigeration and cold chain monitoring system owners and operators to secure remote access to their OT systems. To strengthen system security, owners and operators should review the following resources and implement recommended mitigations:

  • CISA: Primary Mitigations to Reduce Cyber Threats to Operational Technology
  • CISA: Defend the Edge: The Critical Importance of Edge Device Security
  • CISA: Internet Exposure Reduction Guidance
  • United Kingdom’s National Cyber Security Centre and Partners: Secure Connectivity Principles for OT

Contact Information

The authoring organizations recommend U.S. organizations report suspicious or criminal activity related to information provided in this fact sheet:

  • Contact CISA via CISA’s 24/7 Operations Center at contact@cisa.dhs.gov or 1-844-Say-CISA (1-844-729-2472). For more information on reporting a cyber incident, refer to CISA’s Voluntary Cyber Incident Reporting web page. File a claim with FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3) or contact your local FBI field office. When available, please include the following information regarding the incident:
    • Date, time, and location of the incident;
    • Type of activity;
    • Number of people affected;
    • Type of equipment used for the activity; and
    • Name of the submitting company or organization, and a designated point of contact.
  • Contact HHS via HHSCyber@hhs.gov or the HHS 24/7 Operations Center at 202-619-7800 for assistance mitigating potential disruptions to the delivery of healthcare resulting from health and medical supply chain impacts.

Disclaimer

The information in this report is being provided “as is” for informational purposes only. The authoring organizations do not endorse any commercial entity, product, company, or service, including any entities, products, or services linked within this document. Any reference to specific commercial entities, products, processes, or services by service mark, trademark, manufacturer, or otherwise, does not constitute or imply endorsement, recommendation, or favor by the authoring organizations.

item.title: Post-Quantum Questions to Ask Your Vendors
item.description:
CISA, the Australian Signals Directorate’s Australian Cyber Security Centre (ASD’s ACSC) and the National Security Agency (NSA) released joint guidance and an accompanying quick-reference list to help organizations assess vendor readiness for transitioning to post-quantum cryptography (PQC). As quantum computing advances, widely used public-key cryptography will become vulnerable to compromise from cryptographically relevant quantum computers (CRQCs). To protect their systems and data, organizations must plan for and transition to PQC—which includes algorithms capable of withstanding both classical computing and quantum-enabled threats—before CRQCs become available. 

Many organizations rely on third-party vendors for managed services, cloud capabilities, and other cryptography-dependent products and services. Cryptography is also embedded in systems and devices that are difficult to update, tied to long asset lifecycles, and require vendor support or replacement—such as industrial control systems and Internet of Things (IoT) devices. Reliance on vendors means that effective PQC transition depends on vendor readiness, and early, structured engagement with these vendors is critical to planning efforts. 

Organizations can use the vendor-neutral questions outlined in this guidance to determine whether a vendor understands quantum-related risks, maintains transparency over its cryptographic implementations, and supports a secure, cost-effective and timely transition to PQC. 

Visit CISA’s PQC Initiative page for additional resources.

General Mitigation Factors

Recommended security practices and firewall configurations can help protect an industrial control system network from attacks that originate from outside the network. Such practices include that process control systems are physically protected from direct access by unauthorized personnel, have no direct connections to the Internet, and are separated from other networks by means of a firewall system that has a minimal number of ports exposed, and others that have to be evaluated case by case. Industrial control systems should not be used for Internet surfing, instant messaging, or receiving e-mails. Portable computers and removable storage media should be carefully scanned for viruses before they are connected to a control system. Additional information on Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices can be found in the Hitachi Energy’s “Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity Best Practices” Cybersecurity Notification. item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Hitachi Energy is aware of OS command injection and Dirty Frag vulnerabilities that affect CoreTec product versions listed in this document. Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could result in impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability of the product. Please refer to the Recommended Immediate Actions for information about the mitigation/remediation.

The following versions of Hitachi Energy CoreTec Product are affected:

  • CoreTec5 vers:CoreTec5/<=3.4.0, 5.0.0 (CVE-2026-13162, CVE-2026-43284)
  • CoreTec4 vers:CoreTec4/<=3.4.0 (CVE-2026-13162)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 8.8 Hitachi Energy CoreTec5
2 Vulnerabilities
Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection'), Write-what-where Condition

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Energy
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Switzerland

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-13162
An OS command vulnerability exists in CoreTec product that allows authenticated users with certain roles to execute arbitrary system commands with full control over the device. The vulnerability exists in the configuration daemon's time synchronization handler, which is responsible for setting the system timezone. When processing timezone configuration updates, the daemon constructs a shell command by concatenating user-supplied input without any sanitization or validation.
Read More

2 Affected Products

CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended

Remediations

Vendor fix
Update to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0

CoreTec4 versions 3.4.0 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended

Remediations

Vendor fix
Upgrade to CoreTec5 version 5.0.0

Mitigation
Follow general mitigation factors

Additional Metrics

Relevant CWE: CWE-78 Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')

CVSS Version Base Score Base Severity Vector String
3.1 7.5 HIGH CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H
4.0 7.7 HIGH CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:H/AT:N/PR:L/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-43284
A vulnerability exists in the IPsec ESP subsystem (esp4) of the Linux kernel used in CoreTec5 that allows a local unprivileged user to escalate privileges to root. The flaw exists in how the kernel handles memory pages when processing ESP encrypted network packets. An attacker can craft a packet that causes the kernel to decrypt data directly into memory pages it does not own, including cached copies of privileged operating system binaries. When one of those binaries is executed, the attacker's injected code runs with root privileges. In CoreTec5, the vulnerable ESP component is compiled in kernel as a built-in and is present at boot time allowing a local user to exploit it.
Read More

3 Affected Products

CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended

Vendor fix

Remediations
CoreTec5 versions 3.4.0 and prior

Product Status: fixed, known_affected, recommended

Mendix SAML module contains an authentication bypass vulnerability that could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to gain unauthorized access by replaying a valid SAML assertion in IdP-initiated authentication flows. Siemens has released new versions for the affected products and recommends to update to the latest versions.

The following versions of Siemens Mendix SAML Module are affected:

item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary code (CVE-2023-4863), bypass authentication (CVE-2026-16436 and CVE-2026-16437), or perform arbitrary operations (CVE-2026-16438), resulting in information disclosure, tampering with, destruction, or deletion of information, and a denial-of-service (DoS) condition of the system.

The following versions of Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, HyperHistorian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, MC Works64, GENESIS32, BizViz, Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, HyperHistorian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, GENESIS32 and BizViz are affected:

  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions GENESIS64 >=10.97|<=10.97.2 (CVE-2023-4863)
  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions ICONICS Suite >=10.97|<=10.97.2 (CVE-2023-4863)
  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions GENESIS <=11.03 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437)
  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions GENESIS64 <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions ICONICS Suite <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions Hyper Historian <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions AnalytiX <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions MobileHMI <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions IoTWorX <=10.97.3 (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437)
  • Mitsubishi Electric MC Works64 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437, CVE-2026-16438)
  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions GENESIS32 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437)
  • Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions BizViz vers:all/* (CVE-2026-16436, CVE-2026-16437)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 9.1 Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, HyperHistorian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, MC Works64, GENESIS32, BizViz, Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, HyperHistorian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, GENESIS32 and BizViz
3 Vulnerabilities
Out-of-bounds Write, Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password, Incorrect Privilege Assignment

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Japan, United States

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2023-4863
Out-of-bounds Write (CWE-787) vulnerability caused by libwebp, an internal component in GENESIS64 and ICONICS Suite could allow an authenticated local attacker to cause a heap-based buffer overflow and execute arbitrary code by importing a crafted file as an administrator for the affected product. As a result, the attacker may disclose internal information, tamper with, destroy, or delete internal information, or cause the affected system to enter a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.
Read More

4 Affected Products

Mitsubishi Electric GENESIS64: >=10.97|<=10.97.2

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Mitsubishi Electric is releasing fixed version 10.97.3 or later for GENESIS64 and ICONICS Suite. Please download the fixed version from the link below and install it: "https://iconicsinc.my.site.com/community/s/resource-center/product-downloads". (Note: GENESIS64 is included in the ICONICS Suite installation.) For more information on the fixed version, please refer to the Mitsubishi Electric security advisory at "https://www.mitsubishielectric.com/psirt/vulnerability/pdf/2026-006_en.pdf".

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend configuring the PCs with the affected product installed so that only an administrator can log in, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend using the PCs with the affected product installed in the LAN and blocking remote login from untrusted networks and hosts, and from non-administrator users, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend blocking unauthorized access by using a firewall, virtual private network (VPN), etc. and allowing remote login only to administrator when internet access is required, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend restricting physical access to the PC with the affected product installed and the network to which the PC is connected, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend preventing the user from clicking on web links in emails from untrusted sources, or from opening attachments in untrusted emails, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers using the affected product who cannot immediately update it, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend installing anti-virus software on the PC with the affected product installed, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-16436
Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password (CWE-640) vulnerability in GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, MC Works64, GENESIS32, and BizViz could allow a remote attacker to unlock the system by obtaining the challenge response by some means. The challenge response used to unlock the system is common to all users and fixed. As a result, the attacker may disclose, tamper with, destroy, or delete internal information, or cause the affected system to enter a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend installing anti-virus software on the PC with the affected product installed, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend performing the following steps for GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI and MC Works64, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability. (1) Delete the .dat file at the location specified below. This file name and location is different depending on the product version. (Version 10: C:\Program Files\ICONICS\GENESIS64\Components\ClientChallengeTable.dat; Version 11: C:\ProgramData\ICONICS\11\SecurityChallenges.dat) (2) Create a blank file with the same name and location. (3) Restrict the file system write and delete access to this file to a unique administrator account, different than the GENESIS administrator account.

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-16437
Weak Password Recovery Mechanism for Forgotten Password (CWE-640) vulnerability in GENESIS, GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, IoTWorX, MC Works64, GENESIS32, and BizViz could allow an authenticated local user with administrative privileges to unlock the system by tampering with the management file that stores the challenge response. Administrators are able to read and write the management file. But the management file is protected by Windows. As a result, the attacker may disclose, tamper with, destroy, or delete internal information, or cause the affected system to enter a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

View CVE Details

CVE-2026-16438
Incorrect Privilege Assignment (CWE-266) vulnerability in GENESIS64, ICONICS Suite, Hyper Historian, AnalytiX, MobileHMI, and MC Works64 could allow an attacker who can log in using the same administrator account for the affected products to launch and operate DCOM objects locally or remotely. During installation, the installers of the affected products unnecessarily grant default DCOM permissions to the administrator account of the affected products. As a result, the attacker may disclose, tamper with, destroy, or delete internal information, or cause the affected system to enter a denial-of-service (DoS) condition.

For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend configuring the PCs with the affected product installed so that only an administrator can log in, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend using the PCs with the affected product installed in the LAN and blocking remote login from untrusted networks and hosts, and from non-administrator users, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend blocking unauthorized access by using a firewall, virtual private network (VPN), etc. and allowing remote login only to administrator when internet access is required, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend restricting physical access to the PC with the affected product installed and the network to which the PC is connected, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend using the PCs with the affected product installed in the LAN and blocking access from untrusted networks and hosts through firewalls, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation
For customers of products that do not have a fixed version or who cannot immediately update the product, Mitsubishi Electric and Mitsubishi Electric Iconics Digital Solutions recommend blocking unauthorized access by using a firewall, virtual private network (VPN), etc. when internet access is required, to minimize the risk of exploitation of this vulnerability.

Mitigation

Acknowledgments

  • Mitsubishi Electric discovered these vulnerabilities.

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

Advisory Conversion Disclaimer

This ICSA is a verbatim republication of Mitsubishi Electric 2026-006 from a direct conversion of the vendor's Common Security Advisory Framework (CSAF) advisory. This is republished to CISA's website as a means of increasing visibility and is provided "as-is" for informational purposes only. item.dc:creator: CISA

item.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
item.description:
CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

  • CVE-2026-48356 Adobe Commerce and Magento Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-111497 Google Brotli Unchecked Return Value Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. 

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. 

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. 

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Successful exploitation of these vulnerabilities could allow an attacker to cause a denial-of-service condition, corrupt memory, disclose sensitive information, or potentially execute arbitrary code.

The following versions of EPICS Base are affected:

  • EPICS Base release <=7.0.10 (CVE-2026-114595, CVE-2026-114596, CVE-2026-114597, CVE-2026-114598)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 9.8 The EPICS Community EPICS Base release
3 Vulnerabilities
Integer Overflow or Wraparound, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion')

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Global

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2026-114595
In EPICS Base release 7.0.10 and prior, an integer overflow in network request processing can cause memory to be allocated with an incorrect size. Subsequent handling of attacker supplied data may result in memory corruption, denial of service, or potential remote code execution.
Read More

1 Affected Product

The EPICS Community EPICS Base release: <=7.0.10

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation
The EPICS Community has made available updates to the epics-base GitHub repositories. Affected users should update to the 7.0.11 release. For more information, users should contact the EPICS Controls team https://epics-controls.org/support/.

Mitigation
https://github.com/epics-base/epics-base/pull/937

Mitigation

Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

CISA also recommends users take the following measures to protect themselves from social engineering attacks:

  • Do not click web links or open attachments in unsolicited email messages.
  • Refer to Recognizing and Avoiding Email Scams for more information on avoiding email scams.
  • Refer to Avoiding Social Engineering and Phishing Attacks for more information on social engineering attacks.

No known public exploitation specifically targeting these vulnerabilities has been reported to CISA at this time.

item.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
item.description:
CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog and updated the PHP Alert, Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP Require Immediate Patching:  

  • CVE-2026-109618 – PHP Memory Corruption Vulnerability 
  • CVE-2026-109619 – PHP Stale Internal Request-State Vulnerability 

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. 

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. 

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. 

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

item.title: Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Multiple vulnerabilities have been identified in the additional GNU/Linux subsystem of the firmware version V3.1.7 for the SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP (incl. SIPLUS variant). Siemens is preparing fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518(F)-4 PN/DP MFP are affected:

  • SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AB0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7
  • SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AC0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 
  • SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518F-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4FX00-1AB0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 
  • SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518F-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4FX00-1AC0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 
  • SIPLUS S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6AG1518-4AX00-4AC0) vers:intdot/>=3.1.7 
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 10 Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 CPU 1518-4 PN/DP MFP (6ES7518-4AX00-1AB0)
428 Vulnerabilities
Access of Resource Using Incompatible Type ('Type Confusion'), Access of Uninitialized Pointer, Active Debug Code, Buffer Access with Incorrect Length Value, Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow'), Buffer Underwrite ('Buffer Underflow'), Concurrent Execution using Shared Resource with Improper Synchronization ('Race Condition'), Deadlock, Divide By Zero, Expired Pointer Dereference, Exposure of Sensitive Information Due to Incompatible Policies, Exposure of Sensitive Information in Shared Microarchitectural Structures during Transient Execution, Improper Enforcement of Behavioral Workflow, Improper Following of Specification by Caller, Improper Handling of Invalid Use of Special Elements, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, Improper Handling of Missing Special Element, Improper Handling of Structural Elements, Improper Input Validation, Improper Locking, Improper Neutralization of Null Byte or NUL Character, Improper Null Termination, Improper Privilege Management, Improper Resource Locking, Improper Resource Shutdown or Release, Improper Update of Reference Count, Improper Validation of Specified Index, Position, or Offset in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input, Improperly Implemented Security Check for Standard, Incomplete Cleanup, Incomplete Internal State Distinction, Incorrect Calculation of Buffer Size, Incorrect Conversion between Numeric Types, Incorrect Privilege Assignment, Incorrect Synchronization, Incorrect Type Conversion or Cast, Integer Overflow or Wraparound, Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop'), Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value, Misinterpretation of Input, Missing Critical Step in Authentication, Missing Default Case in Multiple Condition Expression, Missing Encryption of Sensitive Data, Missing Initialization of Resource, Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime, Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime, Missing Report of Error Condition, Missing Synchronization, Multiple Releases of Same Resource or Handle, NULL Pointer Dereference, Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release, Out-of-bounds Read, Out-of-bounds Write, Plaintext Storage of a Password, Race Condition within a Thread, Reachable Assertion, Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference, Signal Handler Race Condition, Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition, Transmission of Private Resources into a New Sphere ('Resource Leak'), Trust of System Event Data, Unchecked Return Value, Uncontrolled Recursion, Untrusted Pointer Dereference, Use After Free, Use of Externally-Controlled Format String, Use of Uninitialized Resource, Use of Uninitialized Variable, Write-what-where Condition

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

CVE-2021-41617
sshd in OpenSSH 6.2 through 8.x before 8.8, when certain non-default configurations are used, allows privilege escalation because supplemental groups are not initialized as expected. Helper programs for AuthorizedKeysCommand and AuthorizedPrincipalsCommand may run with privileges associated with group memberships of the sshd process, if the configuration specifies running the command as a different user.

General Recommendations

As a general security measure, Siemens strongly recommends protecting network access to devices with appropriate mechanisms. In order to operate the devices in a protected IT environment, Siemens recommends configuring the environment according to Siemens' operational guidelines for Industrial Security (https://www.siemens.com/cert/operational-guidelines-industrial-security), and to follow the recommendations in the product manuals. Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the exploitation risk of this vulnerability.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, and ensure they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolate them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most recent version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as its connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.

item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Multiple vulnerabilities have been identified in the additional GNU/Linux subsystem of the SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP V1.1.1. Siemens is preparing fixes and recommends specific mitigations for products where fixes are not or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP are affected:

  • SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP - GNU/Linux subsystem vers:all/* 
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 10 Siemens SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP - GNU/Linux subsystem
377 Vulnerabilities
Access of Uninitialized Pointer, Buffer Copy without Checking Size of Input ('Classic Buffer Overflow'), Deadlock, Detection of Error Condition Without Action, Double Free, Expired Pointer Dereference, Heap-based Buffer Overflow, Improper Control of Resource Identifiers ('Resource Injection'), Improper Control of a Resource Through its Lifetime, Improper Handling of Length Parameter Inconsistency, Improper Handling of Missing Special Element, Improper Handling of Structural Elements, Improper Input Validation, Improper Locking, Improper Resource Locking, Improper Restriction of Operations within the Bounds of a Memory Buffer, Improper Update of Reference Count, Improper Validation of Array Index, Improper Validation of Consistency within Input, Improper Validation of Specified Index, Position, or Offset in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Quantity in Input, Improper Validation of Specified Type of Input, Incorrect Synchronization, Integer Overflow or Wraparound, Integer Underflow (Wrap or Wraparound), Loop with Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop'), Missing Default Case in Multiple Condition Expression, Missing Initialization of Resource, Missing Lock Check, Missing Release of Memory after Effective Lifetime, Missing Release of Resource after Effective Lifetime, Multiple Locks of a Critical Resource, NULL Pointer Dereference, Operation on a Resource after Expiration or Release, Out-of-bounds Read, Out-of-bounds Write, Plaintext Storage of a Password, Release of Invalid Pointer or Reference, Return of Wrong Status Code, Signal Handler Race Condition, Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition, Unchecked Return Value, Use After Free, Use of Incorrect Operator, Use of Uninitialized Resource, Write-what-where Condition

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

Expand All +
CVE-2023-52927
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: netfilter: allow exp not to be removed in nf_ct_find_expectation Currently nf_conntrack_in() calling nf_ct_find_expectation() will remove the exp from the hash table. However, in some scenario, we expect the exp not to be removed when the created ct will not be confirmed, like in OVS and TC conntrack in the following patches. This patch allows exp not to be removed by setting IPS_CONFIRMED in the status of the tmpl.
Read More

1 Affected Product

SIMATIC S7-1500 TM MFP - GNU/Linux subsystem

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation
Limit access to the interactive shell of the additional GNU/Linux subssytem to trusted personnel only.

Mitigation
Only build and run applications from trusted sources.

None available
Currently no fix is available

Additional Metrics

Relevant CWE: CWE-20 Improper Input Validation

item.title: Siemens Capital Embedded AR Classic
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

The products listed below contain an out-of-bounds read vulnerability that could allow an attacker to cause abnormal product behavior, instability, or denial of service. Siemens has released a new version for Capital Embedded AR Classic R20-11 and recommends updating to the latest version. Siemens is preparing further fix versions and recommends specific countermeasures for products where fixes are not, or not yet available.

The following versions of Siemens Capital Embedded AR Classic are affected:

  • Capital Embedded AR Classic 431-422 vers:all/* (CVE-2026-89208)
  • Capital Embedded AR Classic R20-11 vers:intdot/<2303 (CVE-2026-89208)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 5.3 Siemens Capital Embedded AR Classic 431-422
1 Vulnerability
Out-of-bounds Read

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Transportation Systems, Energy, Healthcare and Public Health, Financial Services, Government Services and Facilities
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Germany

Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-89208
The affected product does not properly validate input bounds before accessing packet data. This could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to trigger memory reads outside the intended packet boundaries.
Read More

2 Affected Products

Capital Embedded AR Classic 431-422

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation
Apply network segmentation and put the ECUs behind properly configured gateways/firewalls

No fix planned
Currently no fix is planned

Capital Embedded AR Classic R20-11 < V2303

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation
Apply network segmentation and put the ECUs behind properly configured gateways/firewalls

Vendor fix
Update to V2303 or later version

Recommended Practices

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

CISA reminds organizations to perform proper impact analysis and risk assessment prior to deploying defensive measures.

CISA also provides a section for control systems security recommended practices on the ICS webpage on cisa.gov/ics. Several CISA products detailing cyber defense best practices are available for reading and download, including Improving Industrial Control Systems Cybersecurity with Defense-in-Depth Strategies.

CISA encourages organizations to implement recommended cybersecurity strategies for proactive defense of ICS assets.

Additional mitigation guidance and recommended practices are publicly available on the ICS webpage at cisa.gov/ics in the technical information paper, ICS-TIP-12-146-01B--Targeted Cyber Intrusion Detection and Mitigation Strategies.

Organizations observing suspected malicious activity should follow established internal procedures and report findings to CISA for tracking and correlation against other incidents.
